hints: Look closely at the top calibration view. How many eyepiece graticule divisions line up exactly with one 0.1 mm division of the graduated slide?
Measure a grown pollen tube in diagram 2 in eyepiece units, then use your calibration value to convert to micrometres before dividing by 4 hours.
walkthrough:
**Calibrate the eyepiece graticule**

Think of this like working out what one tick on your ruler really means. In the top view the fine 0 to 100 scale is the eyepiece.

One big stage division (0.1 mm) lines up with 50 eyepiece divisions. So:
$$50 \text{ eyepiece units} = 0.1 \text{ mm} = 100 \, \mu\text{m}$$
$$1 \text{ eyepiece unit} = 100 / 50 = 2 \, \mu\text{m}$$

**Measure the pollen tube growth**

At the start in diagram 1 the tubes are just tiny buds, so starting length is almost zero. After 4 hours in diagram 2 a typical tube is about 10 eyepiece units long.

Convert that to a real length:
$$10 \times 2 \, \mu\text{m} = 20 \, \mu\text{m}$$

**Calculate growth rate**

Rate is simply growth divided by time.
$$\text{rate} = \text{length} / \text{time} = 20 \, \mu\text{m} / 4 \text{ h} = 5 \, \mu\text{m} \text{h}^{-1}$$

options.A: Correct. 20 micrometres of growth in 4 hours gives 5 micrometres per hour.
options.B: Too high by double. This forgets to divide correctly or misreads the tube as 20 eyepiece units instead of about 10.
options.C: Wrong units. Millimetres are 1000 times larger than micrometres, the tube is only about 20 micrometres long.
options.D: Wrong on both size and units. This confuses mm for micrometres and overestimates the length.
